adherence.reason: The text is presented as a story set within the Apollo-era Space Race and uses historical figures, institutions, and period context.
Elara is explicitly a seamstress who hand-stitches a spacesuit intended to protect the man who will wear it in space.
The Apollo 1 and moonshot setting places the action during the height of the 1960s Space Race.

Elara understands that one loose stitch could kill in vacuum and checks the featured seam eleven times, but the text says eleven checks are only her habit for high-stress areas and that the neck ring gets twelve, so it does not establish eleven checks for every seam.
The opening and repeated countdown references explicitly place the story forty-eight hours before a scheduled launch and carry the action through the following noon.
The prohibited word does not appear in the story text.
Supervisor Miller identifies a questionable right-forearm seam near the glove interface and threatens to scrap the suit and begin a fresh unit.
Overnight, Elara secretly adds three reinforcing rows to that exact seam, omits the work from the log, and presents the suit without telling Miller.
